newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SOUTH KOREA ANNOUNCES FINAL FINANCIAL REFORM DRAFT.
newsitem.headline: SOUTH KOREA ANNOUNCES FINAL FINANCIAL REFORM DRAFT.

text.p: South Korea's finance minister Kang Kyong-shik said on Monday the central bank governor would be asked to set annual inflation and other macroeconomic targets and would be held responsible for meeting those targets.
Kang, announcing the government's final draft for financial industry reforms, also said the Bank of Korea Governor would replace the finance minister as the chairman of the Monetary Board.
Also attending the news conference were Bank of Korea Governor Lee Kyung-shick and chairman of the Presidential Commission for Financial Reform Park Seong-yawng.
Kang said the draft had been finalised after consultations with Lee and Park, and that the three organisations would have further negotiations on details.
The three existing supervisory bodies for the banking, securities and insurance sectors will be integrated into a unified organisation under the Prime Minister.
Depriving the central bank of its supervisory authority over banks has been a key issue since the presidential commission was formed in January to reform the local financial industry.
The Bank of Korea's labour union on Sunday vowed to oust the governor for agreeing to give up the bank's watchdog role.
The unions of the three watchdog bodies also decided to seek joint labor action on the reform package.

Kang made no mention of another hot issue, the individual ownership limit for banks. It is now set at four percent, but the commission said it could rise to 10 percent under certain conditions. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727-5646 Monday, 16 June 1997 01:52:34 ENDS nSEO7641
